text: Five quick ones. Supervised learning maps inputs to labels. Unsupervised finds structure without them, as in clustering. Reinforcement learning has an agent learn by trial and error, maximizing reward. For regression, MSE, or MAE for robustness to outliers, or Huber, which blends them. For classification, binary cross-entropy, or categorical cross-entropy with softmax. For ranking, hinge, contrastive or triplet loss. k-means assigns each point to the nearest centroid, moves each centroid to its points' mean, and repeats to a local minimum, so run several starts, and pick k by the elbow or the silhouette. It assumes round clusters: on stretched ones, about one point in five lands wrong. One-hot encoding gives each category its own column of zeros and ones, implying no order: red, green and blue become three columns. Set to ignore unknowns, it encodes purple, unseen in training, as all zeros, not an error at serving time. For thousands of values, use hashing or embeddings. Feature engineering turns raw data into useful inputs: interactions, the hour or weekday, logs of skewed values, bins, rolling aggregates. Good features often matter more than the algorithm. Each of these is a few lines of NumPy, and the coding round asks you to write them, fast and safely. Next: coding for machine learning.
